stem: Phosphate is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phosphate is the major inorganic anion in the internal environment.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MAINTENANCE OF A NORMAL INTRA- & EXTRACELLULAR ENVIRONMENT IS FUNDAMENTAL TO LIFE > The Ionic Compositions of Intracellular & Extracellular Fluids Differ Greatly

stem: Phosphoglycerides require which substance?
rationale: Phosphoglycerides consist of a glycerol-phosphate backbone. Two fatty acids are attached to the glycerol-phosphate backbone in ester linkages.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MEMBRANES ARE COMPLEX STRUCTURES COMPOSED OF LIPIDS, PROTEINS, & CARBOHYDRATE-CONTAINING MOLECULES > Phospholipids

stem: Phosphatidic acid is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phosphatidic acid is a 1,2-diacylglycerol 3-phosphate. Phosphatidic acid is a key intermediate in the formation of other phosphoglycerides.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MEMBRANES ARE COMPLEX STRUCTURES COMPOSED OF LIPIDS, PROTEINS, & CARBOHYDRATE-CONTAINING MOLECULES > Phospholipids

stem: Glycerol-phosphate requires which substance?
rationale: In most phosphoglycerides present in membranes, the 3-phosphate is esterified to an alcohol. The alcohol can be choline, ethanolamine, glycerol, inositol, or serine.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MEMBRANES ARE COMPLEX STRUCTURES COMPOSED OF LIPIDS, PROTEINS, & CARBOHYDRATE-CONTAINING MOLECULES > Phospholipids

stem: Fatty acids are converted into which substance?
rationale: A fatty acid is attached by an amide linkage to the amino group of sphingosine, forming ceramide. When the primary hydroxyl group of sphingosine is esterified to phosphorylcholine, sphingomyelin is formed.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MEMBRANES ARE COMPLEX STRUCTURES COMPOSED OF LIPIDS, PROTEINS, & CARBOHYDRATE-CONTAINING MOLECULES > Phospholipids

stem: Hydroxyl is converted into which substance?
rationale: When the primary hydroxyl group of sphingosine is esterified to phosphorylcholine, sphingomyelin is formed. Sphingomyelin is prominent in myelin sheaths.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MEMBRANES ARE COMPLEX STRUCTURES COMPOSED OF LIPIDS, PROTEINS, & CARBOHYDRATE-CONTAINING MOLECULES > Phospholipids

stem: Cholesterol is converted into which substance?
rationale: Cholesterol is the most common sterol in the membranes of animal cells.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MEMBRANES ARE COMPLEX STRUCTURES COMPOSED OF LIPIDS, PROTEINS, & CARBOHYDRATE-CONTAINING MOLECULES > Sterols

stem: Sarcoplasmic reticulum is found within which structure?
rationale: The sarcoplasmic reticulum of muscle cells contains less than a dozen very abundant proteins.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MEMBRANES ARE COMPLEX STRUCTURES COMPOSED OF LIPIDS, PROTEINS, & CARBOHYDRATE-CONTAINING MOLECULES > Different Membranes Have Different Protein Compositions

stem: Phosphatidylserine is found within which structure?
rationale: Phosphatidylserine is preferentially located in the inner leaflet.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MEMBRANES ARE COMPLEX STRUCTURES COMPOSED OF LIPIDS, PROTEINS, & CARBOHYDRATE-CONTAINING MOLECULES > Membranes Are Asymmetric Structures

stem: Phosphatidylethanolamine is found within which structure?
rationale: Phosphatidylethanolamine is preferentially located in the inner leaflet.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MEMBRANES ARE COMPLEX STRUCTURES COMPOSED OF LIPIDS, PROTEINS, & CARBOHYDRATE-CONTAINING MOLECULES > Membranes Are Asymmetric Structures

stem: In which structure are peripheral proteins typically found?
rationale: Peripheral proteins are bound to the hydrophilic regions of specific integral proteins and the head groups of phospholipids.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MEMBRANES ARE COMPLEX STRUCTURES COMPOSED OF LIPIDS, PROTEINS, & CARBOHYDRATE-CONTAINING MOLECULES > Membranes Contain Integral & Peripheral Proteins

stem: In which structure is spectrin typically found?
rationale: Spectrin, a cytoskeletal structure within the erythrocyte, is bound to ankyrin.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MEMBRANES ARE COMPLEX STRUCTURES COMPOSED OF LIPIDS, PROTEINS, & CARBOHYDRATE-CONTAINING MOLECULES > Membranes Contain Integral & Peripheral Proteins

stem: Which substance is typically synthesised by a bilayer?
rationale: The lipids in these vesicles form a bilayer. The structures created by the lipids are known as liposomes.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > ARTIFICIAL MEMBRANES BOTH ALLOW INVESTIGATORS TO MODEL MEMBRANE FUNCTION AND PROVIDE METHODS FOR THE EFFICIENT FORMATION OF LIPID NANOPARTICLES THAT ARE POTENT DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEMS

stem: In which structure are lipid rafts typically found?
rationale: Lipid rafts are specialized areas of the exoplasmic (outer) leaflet of the lipid bilayer enriched in cholesterol, sphingolipids, and certain proteins (Figure 40--8).
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > THE FLUID MOSAIC MODEL OF MEMBRANE STRUCTURE > Lipid Rafts, Caveolae, & Tight Junctions Are Specialized Features of Plasma Membranes

stem: In which structure are tight junctions typically found?
rationale: Tight junctions are often located below the apical surfaces of epithelial cells. Tight junctions prevent the diffusion of macromolecules between cells.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > THE FLUID MOSAIC MODEL OF MEMBRANE STRUCTURE > Lipid Rafts, Caveolae, & Tight Junctions Are Specialized Features of Plasma Membranes

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of nephrogenic diabetes insipidus?
rationale: Mutations in the gene encoding AP-2 have been shown to be the cause of one type of nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MEMBRANE SELECTIVITY ALLOWS ADJUSTMENTS OF CELL COMPOSITION & FUNCTION > Aquaporins Are Proteins That Form Water Channels in Certain Membranes

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of cystic fibrosis?
rationale: The CFTR is implicated in the causation of cystic fibrosis.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > ACTIVE TRANSPORT SYSTEMS REQUIRE A SOURCE OF ENERGY

stem: Which structure does myelin form a part of?
rationale: Myelin sheets, formed by Schwann cells, wrap around nerve fibers and provide an electrical insulator that surrounds most of the nerve.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > TRANSMISSION OF NERVE IMPULSES INVOLVES ION CHANNELS & PUMPS

stem: Which substance is transported by glucose transporters?
rationale: In adipocytes and skeletal muscle, glucose enters by a specific transport system (GLUT4). In adipocytes and skeletal muscle, the transport system (GLUT4) is enhanced by insulin.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > TRANSPORT OF GLUCOSE INVOLVES SEVERAL MECHANISMS

stem: Which substance is transported by the LDL-bound LDL receptor complex?
rationale: The cholesterol-containing low-density lipoprotein (LDL) molecule and its receptor are internalized via coated pits containing the LDL receptor. Endocytotic vesicles containing the LDL-bound LDL receptor complex fuse with lysosomes in the cell.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > CELLS TRANSPORT CERTAIN MACROMOLECULES ACROSS THE PLASMA MEMBRANE BY ENDOCYTOSIS & EXOCYTOSIS > Endocytosis Involves Ingestion of Parts of the Plasma Membrane

stem: Which substance is transported by hepatocytes through absorptive pinocytosis?
rationale: A galactosyl receptor on the surface of hepatocytes facilitates the absorptive pinocytosis of asialoglycoproteins from the circulation. Acid hydrolases taken up by absorptive pinocytosis in fibroblasts are recognized by their mannose-6-phosphate moieties.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > CELLS TRANSPORT CERTAIN MACROMOLECULES ACROSS THE PLASMA MEMBRANE BY ENDOCYTOSIS & EXOCYTOSIS > Endocytosis Involves Ingestion of Parts of the Plasma Membrane

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of achondroplasia?
rationale: Achondroplasia (OMIM 100800) results from mutations in the gene encoding the fibroblast growth factor receptor 3.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MUTATIONS AFFECTING MEMBRANE PROTEINS CAUSE DISEASES

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of hypercholesterolemia?
rationale: Familial hypercholesterolemia (OMIM 143890) is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the LDL receptor.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MUTATIONS AFFECTING MEMBRANE PROTEINS CAUSE DISEASES

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of fibrosis?
rationale: Cystic fibrosis (OMIM 219700) arises from mutations in the gene encoding the CFTR protein, a Cl-transporter.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MUTATIONS AFFECTING MEMBRANE PROTEINS CAUSE DISEASES

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of long QT syndrome?
rationale: Congenital long QT syndrome (OMIM 192500) is due to mutations in genes encoding ion channels in the heart.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MUTATIONS AFFECTING MEMBRANE PROTEINS CAUSE DISEASES

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of Wilson disease?
rationale: Wilson disease (OMIM 277900) is attributed to mutations in the gene encoding a copper-dependent ATPase.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MUTATIONS AFFECTING MEMBRANE PROTEINS CAUSE DISEASES

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of I-cell disease?
rationale: I-cell disease (OMIM 252500) results from mutations in the gene encoding GlcNAc phosphotransferase, leading to the absence of the Man 6-P signal for lysosomal localization of certain hydrolases.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MUTATIONS AFFECTING MEMBRANE PROTEINS CAUSE DISEASES

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of hereditary spherocytosis?
rationale: Hereditary spherocytosis (OMIM 182900) is caused by mutations in the genes encoding spectrin or other structural proteins in the red cell membrane.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MUTATIONS AFFECTING MEMBRANE PROTEINS CAUSE DISEASES

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of fat maldigestion?
rationale: Cystic fibrosis causes fat maldigestion due to pancreatic exocrine insufficiency.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MUTATIONS AFFECTING MEMBRANE PROTEINS CAUSE DISEASES > Cystic Fibrosis Is Due to Mutations in the Gene Encoding CFTR, a Chloride Transporter

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of infertility in males?
rationale: Cystic fibrosis leads to infertility in males due to abnormal development of the vas deferens.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview > MUTATIONS AFFECTING MEMBRANE PROTEINS CAUSE DISEASES > Cystic Fibrosis Is Due to Mutations in the Gene Encoding CFTR, a Chloride Transporter

stem: Which structure in a mammalian cell is defined by a membrane?
rationale: The 20 or so membranes in a mammalian cell have different compositions and functions and they define essential compartments, or specialized environments, within the cell that have specific functions.
citation: chapter_40_membranes_structure_and_function — Overview
